content: A night owl refers to an individual who has a tendency to remain awake until late at night. Typically, night owls stay awake well past midnight, with extreme cases remaining awake until 5:00 or 6:00 AM. Some night owls exhibit this behavior due to personal preference or habitual patterns, while others may stay awake late to accommodate working night shifts. Individuals who experience significant difficulty in adjusting to conventional sleeping and waking schedules may suffer from a condition known as Delayed Sleep Phase Syndrome (DSPS). This condition is characterized by a misalignment of the individual's internal circadian rhythm with societal norms for sleep and wake times. A preference for the nighttime or darker environments is referred to as nyctophilia or scotophilia. The opposite of a night owl is commonly referred to as an early bird or lark. Early birds tend to go to sleep at what is considered an early hour, allowing them to wake up early in the morning. In some cultures, early birds are labeled as A-people, while night owls are referred to as B-people. In scientific research, the terms morningness and eveningness are used to describe these chronotypes. Notable individuals who have been described as night owls include Winston Churchill, Bill Clinton, Glenn Gould, Elvis Presley, Marcel Proust, and J.R.R. Tolkien.
